findings.claim: Real sensor dropouts are independent of the state and of the noise, as assumed here
findings.value: not established: the dropout pattern is declared and state-independent

hypothesis: A missing reading is handled by prediction only: the covariance grows exactly by the model and the filter stays consistent; any substituted value (zero, hold-last) is refused because it fabricates information.
input_data: 47 missing ticks (block 30-59 plus 20% random), shared by all runs
mathematical_model: P(k + n | k) = F(n dt) P F(n dt)^T + Q(n dt) with F(t) = [[I, t I], [0, I]], Q(t) = q [[t^3/3 I, t^2/2 I], [t^2/2 I, t I]]; the position variance gains q (n dt)^3 / 3 plus the propagated terms. dt = 0.1 s, q = 0.05.
numerical_result: max relative growth error 8.6e-16; ANEES inside 1.00 of ticks; gap-end |z| 2.20; position variance grows 86x over the gap; zero-fill grand NEES 2306 (exact prediction 2281), RMSE 3.77 m vs 0.459 m.
observation_model: Camera position when present; absent otherwise (no placeholder value exists).

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.

uncertainty: Closed-form comparison is exact to roundoff; Monte Carlo statements carry 99% per-tick intervals and a Bonferroni bound on the gap-end covariance.
unresolved_assumptions: Dropouts are missing at random; state-dependent dropouts (occlusion near obstacles) bias the filter even with prediction-only steps.

A caller who builds an Observation with value (0, 0) is indistinguishable from a genuine reading at the origin: the API refuses requested substitutes, not zero-filling done before an Observation is constructed.
Long gaps stay consistent only while the motion model holds (see T073).
